record.context_brief: Gram dimension and van der Holst parameter
record.original_question: For a graph G, let gd(G) be the Gram dimension: the smallest integer k >= 1 such that every vector family p_1,...,p_n admits vectors q_1,...,q_n in R^k preserving all vertex squared norms and all inner products on edges. Let nu_equal(G) be the van der Holst parameter defined as the maximum corank of a positive semidefinite matrix M in the cone C(G) of matrices with zero entries on nonedges, subject to the Strong Arnold Property. Is gd(G) <= nu_equal(G), so that gd(G) and nu_equal(G) coincide given the known inequality gd(G) >= nu_equal(G)?

evidence.quote: The Gram dimension gd(G) is defined as the smallest integer k >= 1 such that, for every family of vectors p1,...,pn, there exists another family of vectors q1,...,qn in Rk satisfying squared norms and edge inner products.
Problem 4. Determine the validity of the inequality gd(G) <= nu_equal(G), relating the Gram dimension gd(G) and the van der Holst parameter nu_equal(G).
The parameter nu_equal(G) is defined as the maximum corank of a matrix M in C(G) satisfying the Strong Arnold Property.
Our second problem asks for the validity of the converse inequality. In other words, is it true that the two graph parameters gd(.) and nu_equal(.) coincide?

artifact.category_tag: Graph parameters and PSD matrix completion
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph with V = {1, 2, ..., n}.

(1) Gram dimension. For an integer k >= 1, say that G has Gram dimension at most k if, for every family of vectors p_1, ..., p_n in some Euclidean space, there exists a family of vectors q_1, ..., q_n in R^k such that
  - ||q_i||^2 = ||p_i||^2 for every i in V, and
  - <q_i, q_j> = <p_i, p_j> for every edge {i, j} in E.
Define gd(G) to be the smallest such integer k.

(2) van der Holst parameter. Let S^n denote the space of real symmetric n x n matrices, and let
  C(G) = { M in S^n : M is positive semidefinite, and M_{ij} = 0 whenever i ≠ j and {i, j} is not an edge of G }.
A matrix M in S^n is said to satisfy the Strong Arnold Property if the only symmetric n x n matrix X with MX = 0, X_{ii} = 0 for all i, and X_{ij} = 0 whenever {i, j} is an edge of G or i = j, is X = 0.
Define nu_equal(G) to be the maximum corank (dimension of the kernel) of a matrix M in C(G) that also satisfies the Strong Arnold Property.

It is known that gd(G) >= nu_equal(G) for every graph G. 

Question: Does the reverse inequality gd(G) <= nu_equal(G) hold for every graph G? Equivalently, do the two graph parameters gd(·) and nu_equal(·) coincide?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed by Laurent and Varvitsiotis, who established gd(G) >= nu_equal(G) and proved equality for graphs with gd(G) <= 4 via forbidden-minor characterizations (K_5 and K_{2,2,2}). Subsequent literature, including work on universal completability and least-eigenvalue frameworks, continues to refer to the general inequality/equality question as an open problem; no proof of gd(G) <= nu_equal(G) for all graphs has been located.

status_evidence.title: The Gram dimension of a graph
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes gd(G) and connections to the van der Holst type parameter nu_equal, proving forbidden minor characterization for gd(G) <= 4.
status_evidence.claim: The inequality gd(G) >= nu_equal(G) is established, and the equality is verified only for small cases, leaving the general question open.

status_evidence.title: Positive Semidefinite Matrix Completion, Universal Rigidity and the Strong Arnold Property
status_evidence.snippet: Further studies relating Gram dimension to nu_equal via the Strong Arnold Property.
status_evidence.claim: Continued investigation of the relationship without resolving the equality in general.

status_evidence.title: Universal Completability, Least Eigenvalue Frameworks, and Vector Colorings
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work referencing the Gram dimension and related Colin de Verdière-type parameters.
status_evidence.claim: Later literature still treats the equality of gd and nu_equal as not established in general.
